name: Roman Catholic Distinctives (Gospel Critique)

objectives.text: Identify from Scripture that God saves people by his grace through faith in Jesus and not by the good things they do
Name Jesus as the one mediator between God and people and the one through whom Christians pray to God
Recall that the Bible is God's Word and the highest authority for what Christians believe, above any church leader
Describe how to speak kindly and truthfully with Roman Catholic neighbors while naming that Protestants and Catholics disagree about how a person is saved
Identify beliefs that Protestants and Roman Catholics hold in common, such as the Trinity and the deity and resurrection of Christ, using the Apostles' Creed
Summarize the five solas of the Reformation and a Scripture passage that supports each one
Explain the difference between salvation by grace alone and salvation by grace plus works using Paul's argument in Romans
Compare the repeated sacrifices of the Old Testament priests with the once-for-all sacrifice of Jesus as High Priest
Describe the main events of the Protestant Reformation, including Martin Luther's protest against indulgences and his recovery of justification by faith
Apply the sufficiency of Scripture by testing a church teaching against what the Bible says
Analyze the difference between the Reformed view of Scripture as the supreme authority and the Roman Catholic view of Scripture, Tradition, and the Magisterium together
Compare the Roman Catholic view of justification as a lifelong process with the Reformed view of justification as God's once-for-all legal declaration
Compare Roman Catholic teaching on the Mass as a sacrifice and on transubstantiation with Reformed teaching on the Lord's Supper as a remembrance and sign of Christ's finished work
Compare the seven sacraments of Roman Catholic teaching with the two sacraments confessed in the Reformed tradition
Explain why the Reformed tradition does not receive the Apocrypha as part of the canon of Scripture
Evaluate the Roman Catholic doctrines of purgatory and indulgences in light of the sufficiency of Christ's atonement
Summarize the historical context and main decrees of the Council of Trent on Scripture, tradition, and justification
Analyze the Roman Catholic practice of praying to Mary and the saints, including the distinction between veneration and worship, in light of Christ's sole mediation
Evaluate the doctrines of papal primacy and papal infallibility, including the interpretation of Jesus' words to Peter
Defend the Reformed doctrine of the imputation of Christ's righteousness against the Roman Catholic doctrine of infused righteousness
Evaluate the Marian dogmas of the Immaculate Conception and the Assumption against the teaching of Scripture
Evaluate whether modern ecumenical statements such as the 1999 Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification resolve the Reformation disagreement over the gospel
Create a gracious plan for a conversation with a Roman Catholic friend that explains justification by faith alone from Scripture

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (grace vs works, Christ as mediator, Scripture's authority, five solas, priesthood in Hebrews, authority, justification, Mass, purgatory, Trent, papal infallibility, imputation, Marian dogmas). Recast childish phrasing (chores, Bible as boss) into accurate statements. Merged the vague 'apply sola scriptura' into a concrete task of testing teaching against Scripture. Replaced the 'observe we love our neighbors' item with a describable skill of gracious, truthful conversation. Added missing competencies: shared creedal beliefs, Reformation history, seven vs two sacraments, the Apocrypha and canon, prayer to Mary and saints, modern ecumenical statements, and a culminating conversation plan. Corrected confession citations to full document names and added fitting Westminster and Heidelberg references only where they state the doctrine.
